briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East faces a severe escalation following widespread US strikes against military and infrastructure targets across Iran and Iranian retaliatory attacks on US bases and assets in Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman. This direct and expanding confrontation, coupled with Iran's announced halt to commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, has pushed the region to the brink of a major conflict with significant global economic implications.

IRAN
US forces completed a new wave of offensive strikes on July 12, targeting dozens of locations with precision munitions across Iran, including air defense systems, coastal radar sites, missile and drone capabilities, and small boats around the Strait of Hormuz. Strikes were reported in at least seven provinces, including Khuzestan (Mahshahr, Ahvaz, Omidiyeh, Dezful), Bushehr, Hormozgan (Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, Sirik, Jask), Markazi (Khondab), Isfahan (Na'in), and Lorestan. Casualties include 1 killed and 7 injured in Na'in (Isfahan), 1 killed and 4 injured in Mahshahr (Khuzestan), and a communications manager (Nooh Mahdavi) killed with two others injured on Farvar Island (Hormozgan). Military targets like the Aghajari airport in Omidiyeh, Bakri barracks in Dezful, and Qods barracks in Dezful were reportedly hit, as well as water pumping stations and a telecommunications tower. Iran claims to have shot down a US LUCAS drone near Bandar Abbas.

In retaliation, Iran's Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) announced a "five-phase retaliatory operation" targeting US military bases and assets. Alleged strikes hit fuel depots and ammunition storage facilities at Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan, helicopter overhaul centers and drone command centers at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, two HIMARS launchers and missile depots, Patriot air defense systems, and a strategic FPS radar at Ali Al Salem and Ahmad Al Jaber Air Bases in Kuwait, and long-range air defense and vessel detection radars in Oman. The Iranian Army also launched fresh drone strikes on US positions in Kuwait. The Foreign Ministry spokesman, Asmaeil Bakaii, stated that Iran does not agree to IAEA access to nuclear facilities and will consider any region or country used for attacks against Iran as a legitimate target for defensive actions. He added that the US has violated the Islamabad MoU and committed war crimes by attacking Iranian infrastructure. Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi called for a predefined "crushing and regret-inducing" response to any assassination attempt against Iranian leadership. The country's stock market experienced significant drops.

Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, the newly established Iranian "Gulf Waterway Management Authority" announced a halt to vessel traffic due to "illegal US military movements." The IRGC Navy Commander Ali Ozmaei stated that Iran continuously monitors all foreign vessels and will not allow the Strait to be used to threaten Iran's national security. Oil prices rose, approaching $80 per barrel. Internally, there were reports of students' personal data being leaked on Telegram channels.

ISRAEL
The Israeli Air Force struck a Hamas weapons manufacturing site in Gaza City, stating that "several Hamas terrorists" were operating there in violation of the ceasefire agreement. Separately, the IDF announced the killing of two Hamas operatives last week: Hassan Mustafa Zahir Al-Razina, who tried to plant explosives near the "Yellow Line," and Mohammad Mahmoud Abd al-Mu'ti Fayyoumi, a Nukhba Force member. An interceptor was launched towards a false target in the Western Galilee.

Domestically, a major police operation, involving a Bedouin agent, resulted in the arrest of 34 suspects for illegal arms and drug trafficking. Haifa beaches were closed due to abnormal microbial water quality after sewage discharge. Politically, there is significant tension. MK Avigdor Liberman criticized proposed Haredi draft exemptions and the extension of IDF service, calling it a "severe blow to Israel's security." Legislation to finalize the "Basic Law: Torah Study" and a law to freeze legal proceedings for draft dodgers passed Knesset committees. A controversial law to weaken the Attorney General's role also advanced. Shas MK Haim Biton is under investigation for misusing public education funds. Opposition leader Yair Lapid met with Shin Bet head David Zini. The Knesset is discussing its dissolution, with October 27 proposed as the election date. The "Battle Shocked" law, defining combat veterans' status and benefits, passed committee with bipartisan support. The state withdrew an indictment against Reut Ben Haim, who blocked aid trucks to Gaza.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF conducted airstrikes in Gaza City, targeting a Hamas weapons manufacturing site that was reportedly being used to restore the organization's capabilities in violation of the ceasefire agreement, killing "several Hamas terrorists." Palestinian media reported four fatalities from this strike. Earlier last week, the IDF killed two Hamas operatives, Hassan Mustafa Zahir Al-Razina and Mohammad Mahmoud Abd al-Mu'ti Fayyoumi, identified as posing an immediate threat.

The humanitarian situation in northern Gaza deteriorated as the UN reported that Hamas forcefully seized a World Food Programme (WFP) food distribution center in Jabalia, halting food aid to thousands of families and violently attacking aid truck drivers. COGAT warned Gaza residents that Hamas is actively stealing humanitarian aid for its own interests. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers attacked independent journalists and a CNN crew in Sinjil. The EU Foreign Ministers are scheduled to discuss a possible import ban on goods from Israeli settlements, considering options such as licenses, high tariffs, or an outright prohibition.

LEBANON
The IDF uncovered a Hezbollah lair, including tunnels and an underground surgical room, beneath the strategic Beaufort bulwark, describing it as a "terror nest." Lebanese media reported an Israeli Air Force targeted strike in Sar'in, South Lebanon. IDF Reserve Battalion 6828 is stationed at the location where Eldad Regev and Ehud Goldwasser were abducted 20 years ago, highlighting ongoing tensions on the border.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Syrian Parliament convened for the first time since the fall of the Assad regime. In Iraq, an Iranian drone attack was reported on a Kurdish-Iranian opposition camp in the northern Sulaymaniyah province. The Iraqi Parliament is set to host officials to discuss the death of an Iraqi fisherman and naval force commander, implying potential spillover from regional tensions. Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia' Al Sudani departed for Washington to discuss oil and gas issues and explore ways to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz.

GULF STATES
The Gulf States are experiencing direct impacts from the US-Iran confrontation. Bahrain reported multiple alarms activated and explosions, with the Interior Ministry urging citizens to seek shelter. IRGC claims to have destroyed US military infrastructure at Sheikh Isa Air Base and a US Navy Fifth Fleet support facility in Jufair, supported by satellite imagery showing damage and smoke plumes. Kuwait confirmed its military is on "full readiness" after suffering attacks on three land border posts and an offshore drilling platform of Kuwait Oil Company, which injured one worker. The Kuwaiti military also dealt with "hostile aerial targets" in its airspace, and Patriot air defense systems were activated. Oman summoned the Iranian ambassador to protest drone attacks that reportedly targeted radar installations. Qatar announced it has again halted tanker movements and recommended suspending marine vessel trips due to the escalating situation, despite having recently resumed operations. Pakistan's Prime Minister is in Doha for a one-day visit, ostensibly to offer condolences for the former Emir, but likely also engaging in diplomatic efforts.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Extensive US Strikes in Iran**: The US launched a new, widespread wave of strikes on July 12, targeting dozens of military, air defense, radar, missile, drone, and critical infrastructure sites across at least seven Iranian provinces (Khuzestan, Bushehr, Hormozgan, Markazi, Isfahan, Lorestan). Casualties include at least 2 killed (1 in Na'in, 1 in Mahshahr) and several injured.
2.  **Iranian Retaliatory Strikes**: Iran's IRGC responded with a "five-phase retaliatory operation" hitting US military bases and assets in Jordan (Prince Hassan Air Base), Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base, US Navy Fifth Fleet support facility), Kuwait (Ali Al Salem, Ahmad Al Jaber Air Bases, Port Shuaiba, 3 border posts, KOC drilling platform), and Oman (radar installations).
3.  **Strait of Hormuz Disruption**: Iran's "Gulf Waterway Management Authority" announced a halt to vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, citing "illegal US military movements." US CENTCOM insists the Strait remains open, but only 6 ships transited on July 12, the lowest in five weeks, and Qatar has halted tanker traffic.
4.  **Direct US-Iran Confrontation in Hormuz**: US CENTCOM confirmed shooting down an Iranian cruise missile and a drone targeting commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM also denied Iranian claims of US casualties in Kuwait.
5.  **Hamas Violations and IDF Strikes in Gaza**: IDF bombed a Hamas weapons manufacturing site in Gaza City, killing "several Hamas terrorists," as Hamas was reportedly rebuilding capabilities in violation of a ceasefire. The IDF also killed two other Hamas operatives (Hassan Al-Razina and Mohammad Fayyoumi) last week.
6.  **Hamas Seizes Humanitarian Aid**: The UN reported Hamas forcefully took control of a WFP food distribution center in Jabalia, North Gaza, halting food aid to thousands and assaulting aid truck drivers.
7.  **Escalating Israeli Internal Political Tensions**: Key legislation advanced in the Knesset, including the "Basic Law: Torah Study," a law to freeze legal proceedings for Haredi draft dodgers, and a law to weaken the Attorney General's role, fueling significant domestic opposition and criticism.
8.  **EU Considers Settlement Import Ban**: EU Foreign Ministers are set to discuss options for imposing an import ban on goods from Israeli settlements, ranging from licensing to an outright prohibition.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of regional escalation is VERY HIGH, with direct military confrontation between the United States and Iran actively underway. The Strait of Hormuz is an immediate flashpoint, with Iran's declaration of a halt to shipping and the US insistence on freedom of navigation leading to direct military encounters involving drones and cruise missiles. Southern Iran and US military bases across the Persian Gulf states are also active flashpoints due to ongoing reciprocal strikes. In Gaza, the continued IDF operations against Hamas, coupled with Hamas's reported ceasefire violations and humanitarian aid seizures, maintains a high level of instability.
Red lines appear to be freedom of navigation in Hormuz for the US, and any direct threats to Iranian national security or leadership for Iran. The widespread nature of US strikes and Iranian retaliatory actions demonstrates a willingness by both sides to engage militarily across a broad geographical area, increasing the potential for miscalculation and wider conflict. Russia has issued a warning against any attack on the Bushehr nuclear plant, highlighting a specific high-risk target.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** confirmed ordering new strikes against Iran to degrade its ability to attack commercial shipping in Hormuz, with President Trump asserting the Strait is open. CENTCOM denied Iranian claims of US casualties in Kuwait and emphasized its forces are "ready for any scenario." The **E3** (UK, France, Germany) issued a joint statement condemning "reckless" Iranian attacks in Hormuz and the Gulf, calling for a ceasefire and a return to US-Iran negotiations, while omitting criticism of US actions. The **EU** is set to discuss a potential ban on imports from Israeli settlements.
**Gulf States** are directly affected: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued shelter warnings, Kuwait placed its military on "full readiness" and confirmed attacks on its territory, and Oman summoned the Iranian ambassador to protest drone strikes. Qatar has halted tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. **Russia** warned that any attack on Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant would be a crime with severe regional consequences, and its Foreign Minister Lavrov reportedly arrived in Tehran. **Iraq's** Prime Minister is traveling to Washington to discuss reducing dependence on Hormuz. **Pakistan** urged all parties to exercise restraint and return to dialogue and diplomacy. **Yemen** reaffirmed support for Iran and warned of harm to the US and global economy if aggression continues.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist. US CENTCOM reports completing a wave of strikes, while Iranian sources describe an ongoing "five-phase retaliatory operation," suggesting differing interpretations of the operational timeline. CENTCOM explicitly denied Iranian claims of US military casualties in Kuwait, but Kuwaiti officials confirmed damage and one injury from drone strikes on their territory. The Strait of Hormuz status remains contested, with Iran declaring it closed and the US asserting it is open, while shipping data indicates significant disruption. Conflicting reports exist on the specific "ceasefire agreements" in violation, one potentially referencing the US-Iran "Islamabad MoU" and the other the Israel-Hamas agreement in Gaza. The extent of damage and casualties from the numerous US strikes in Iran and Iranian counter-strikes is still emerging, with many details unverified or based on local reports. Iranian social media's celebratory and propagandistic tone regarding Lindsey Graham's death stands in contrast to US reports of natural causes. The purpose of Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov's reported visit to Tehran is unconfirmed, but suggests high-level diplomatic engagement amidst the crisis.
